claim: When an app client supports a SAML 2.0 IdP with IdP-initiated sign-in, you can add only other SAML 2.0 IdPs to that app client; the user pool directory and all non-SAML external identity providers cannot be added to it.
question: If an app client accepts IdP-initiated SAML sign-in, which other sign-in options can that app client have?

values.display: you can only add other SAML 2.0 IdPs

values.spoken: no local users and no social or OIDC providers

qualifiers.scope: per app client with IdP-initiated SAML sign-in
qualifiers.condition: a SAML 2.0 IdP that supports IdP-initiated sign-in is active in the app client

evidence.quote: When you activate support for a SAML 2.0 IdP that supports IdP-initiated sign in an app client, you can only add other SAML 2.0 IdPs to that app client. You're prevented from adding the user directory in the user pool *and* all non-SAML external identity providers to an app client configured in this way.

claim: A user pool signs all SAML single logout requests and can be set to sign SAML single sign-on requests to any external SAML IdP; an IdP configured for SAML encryption encrypts its SAML responses with the encryption certificate that Amazon Cognito generates for that provider.
question: Can a Cognito user pool sign SAML requests and receive encrypted SAML responses?

values.display: Your user pool signs all single logout (SLO) requests
encrypt SAML responses with the encryption certificate

qualifiers.scope: SAML identity providers in a Cognito user pool

evidence.quote: Your user pool signs all single logout (SLO) requests, and you can configure your user pool to sign single sign-on (SSO) requests for any SAML external IdP.
Your SAML IdP can encrypt SAML responses with the encryption certificate.

claim: A resource server is an OAuth 2.0 API server that checks that access tokens from the user pool contain the scopes that authorize the requested method and path; custom scopes, which you define on resource servers, authorize requests to the APIs that the resource servers protect.
question: What is a Cognito resource server, and what do custom scopes authorize?

values.display: Custom scopes authorize requests to the external APIs

qualifiers.scope: Cognito user pool resource servers and custom scopes

evidence.quote: A *resource server* is an OAuth 2.0 API server. To secure access-protected resources, it validates that access tokens from your user pool contain the scopes that authorize the requested method and path in the API that it protects.
Custom scopes authorize requests to the external APIs that resource servers protect.

claim: An application that calls an API with machine-to-machine (M2M) authorization must have a client ID and a client secret, so its user pool app client must have a client secret.
question: What credentials does an application need for Cognito machine-to-machine authorization?

values.display: must have a client ID and client secret
values.spoken: a client ID and a client secret

qualifiers.scope: per app client used for M2M authorization

evidence.quote: An application that accesses an API with M2M authorization must have a client ID and client secret. In your user pool, build an app client that has a client secret.
